Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first follow the workspace README, then inspect both wake views using the visual-signals skill, and consult the fish-control bookshelf before proposing the single candidate. After that I’ll trace the parent/inherited evidence, implement in `solver/`, and update both required evidence records.

The contract confirms direct still-water initialization and requires visual comparison before any edit. I’m now anchoring the four sampled keyframe sheets to their observations, metrics, diagnostics, current guidance, and inherited notes; the bookshelf’s source references will be selected only after that evidence points to a mechanism.

The visual evidence is unusually consistent: all four fish self-propel with coherent alternating top-down and compact oblique wakes, and all capture; the discriminating failure is actuator protection, not task semantics. The uncancelled-work governor is the clear finite leader (`17.688T`, `1.96419L` integral), while the signed, dominant-joint, and independently guarded variants trail at `17.99–18.111T`. I’m consulting the bookshelf now because the structured protocol requires it; the edit will transfer only a phase/energy invariant, not gains or kinematics.

The matched policies reveal why the fastest variant is not a clean actuator lesson: its aggregate guard scales the whole two-joint carrier whenever either joint injects energy, so it can also suppress the other joint’s braking/reversal component. That candidate reaches earlier, but has the worst `>99%` anterior rate residence (`12.13%`), the highest sampled planar force/yaw-moment peaks (`0.03198/0.01651`), and a longer `12.330L` path. I’m recording a one-mechanism hypothesis before touching the policy: keep its aggregate uncancelled-work trigger, but withdraw only positive-work carrier components and leave carrier reversal plus all body-frame steering intact.

The policy now contains one candidate only: the evaluated fastest controller’s aggregate uncancelled-work trigger, with a new positive-work/reversal decomposition. No steering, route stage, distance gate, or scalar threshold was added. I’m now replacing the parent’s stale “next test” guidance with the evaluated four-way result and a reusable boundary for later workers.

Both required records are materially updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s mandated check-runner now; it will verify guidance semantics, the parameter/return contract, and the editable boundary without running CFD.

The mandated checker found one repairable workspace defect unrelated to the candidate: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so the semantic guidance comparison cannot identify a unique parent. I’m removing that duplicated marker (the same repair recorded in inherited workers), then rerunning validation. The solver boundary already passes; Julia is not on `PATH`, so I’ll also check whether a workspace/local runtime exists before treating that test as unavailable.

Validation now passes end-to-end: the guidance update is materially distinct from the assigned parent, the Julia contract returns two finite accelerations with every referenced parameter owned, and the solver boundary contains no unauthorized edits. I’m adding that non-CFD validation record to the provenance notes and doing one final consistency audit; no CFD will be run here.

Produced exactly one 3D multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): aggregate uncancelled-work governor that attenuates only positive-work carrier components, preserving reversal and steering.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:72): materially revised reusable carrier-governor lesson.

All mandated checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and solver boundary. No CFD was run.
